simple.meaning: זַלְזַל (zalzal) is a Hebrew word meaning “tremulous , i.e. a twig.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: This word has limited occurrence data, so BibleIQ begins with the Hebrew word, its basic meaning, and the verse where it appears.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to זַלְזַל (H2150) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in זַלְזַל (H2150) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: זַלְזַל (zalzal) / H2150 is traced through Isaiah 18:5 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H2150. zalzal [ זַלְזַל ] noun [masculine] (quivering) tendrils ; — only plural tendrils of vine הַזַּלְזַלִּים Isa 18:5 (|| הַנְּטִישׁוֺת ), in figure of Yahweh's destroying the Assyrians.

occurrences.englishText: For before the harvest, when the blossom is over, and the flower becomes a ripening grape, he will cut off the sprigs with pruning hooks, and he will cut down and take away the spreading branches.
